knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Keeping the glass wet before the squeegee pass stops the blade from dragging grit and leaving streaks. Speed (option 0) and seeing marks (option 2) are not the reason.
A mirror is buffed with a separate dry cloth and inspected at an angle. Reusing the washing cloth (option 0) spreads residue; powder (option 2) is not an approved product.
Above floor-level reach, approved access equipment, a second person and a single climber at any moment all apply. Standing on a chair (options 0 and 2) is not acceptable.

practicalCriteria: Given a glazed pane within easy reach, the learner keeps the glass wet and completes a squeegee sequence in overlapping strokes from the top corner, with the rubber cleared between strokes; the assessor observes the sequence and checks the pane at an angle in good light.
Given a mirror, the learner washes it with a moistened cloth, buffs with a separate dry cloth, and inspects at an angle; the assessor confirms the mirror is streak-free and the frame is clean.

Given a supplied scenario above the floor-level reach, the learner sets up the approved access equipment with a second person in place before any step, and states the one-person-on-ladder rule; the assessor observes the set-up without the learner starting the task before the set-up is complete.
The learner records the area as done and records any defect found, using a supplied record sheet.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Area record and defect report from the observed task
Access equipment check record for the above-reach scenario
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses powder, paste or an abrasive on glass or a mirror
Learner works above the floor-level reach without approved access equipment and a second person
Learner stands on a chair, the top rung of a ladder or any unstable item to reach
